reports.description: Many malware use Bitcoin wallets to retrieve hidden malicious command and control (C&C) IP addresses. However, since initial network connections point to seemingly benign Bitcoin service endpoints, investigators often struggle to understand this type of attack. We conducted a study of 100k malware and found that over 2,800 are using a Bitcoin wallet ID to find their C&C server. This wallet ID was discovered in some of our analyzed samples. The continued operation of the account corresponding to the wallet ID enables the continued proliferation of this botnet. - CyFi Lab (https://cyfi.ece.gatech.edu/).

I mentioned to him that I don‚Äôt have experience in trading, he said I don‚Äôt have to worry about it because he would trade for me and help me. He asked me to use WhatsApp to communicate. After when I deposited my money, he asked me to download any desk and he would guide me through the website. Then he asked me to create a BTC account so I can use BTC to invest, which I had no experience in.  Then we started to trade and a couple of days later I saw that my profit is growing. Then Loic said to invest more money to have better trades and income, so I did. A few days later I saw a decent amount on my account so I asked for a withdraw.
